channel.title: Security on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Security on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Front Door mutual TLS authentication
item.description:
Azure Front Door Premium now supports mutual TLS (mTLS) in general availability. It uses X.509 client certificates for client authentication to help protect sensitive applications and APIs.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents
item.description:
Microsoft describes how poisoned datasets and model checkpoints in the post-training supply chain can compromise coding agents, leading to remote code execution and other malicious behavior. The post is a security analysis from Defender Research and the AI Red Team.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Secret scanning detects Cloudflare service tokens
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning now detects Cloudflare service tokens in repositories. The new detector covers the Cloudflare Access service token secret type.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Rate limit grouping for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
item.description:
Azure Front Door Premium WAF now supports rate limit grouping in public preview. This lets rate limit rules aggregate requests across a group instead of counting only per client IP, which helps with distributed attacks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Secret scanning detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs
item.description:
GitHub secret scanning now detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs. The feature is available in public preview and adds workflow logs to the existing scanning coverage for issues, wikis, discussions, and pull requests.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Front Door TLS key exchange policy with post-quantum support
item.description:
Azure Front Door now offers configurable TLS key exchange policies, including hybrid post-quantum key exchange. This lets you balance cryptographic readiness with client compatibility requirements.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Secret scanning upgrades detectors, adds SpaceX as partner
item.description:
GitHub updated secret scanning by adding SpaceX as a new partner and introducing detection for starlink_public_api_v2_secret. It also upgraded multiple existing detectors, including Alibaba, AWS, Google, OpenVSX, and Pydantic Services.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves accuracy and query metadata
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.4 was released with accuracy improvements across several queries and updates to query metadata. The changelog post does not include further technical detail in the provided excerpt.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Fake-download campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes a fake-download campaign that uses trojanized Inno installers to deliver monetization payloads. The post includes detection and investigation guidance covering the full installer session.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Desktop adds short-lived authentication tokens
item.description:
GitHub Desktop 3.6.10+ now supports short-lived, automatically refreshing authentication tokens for eligible accounts. This reduces the time a leaked token remains usable.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Security risk assessments include repository protection status
item.description:
GitHub’s code security risk assessment and secret risk assessment now indicate whether findings are in protected or unprotected repositories. This helps organizations see where to extend security coverage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: pull_request_target blocked by default December 2
item.description:
Starting December 2, 2026, GitHub Actions will block pull_request_target events by default in all public repositories unless an applicable Actions event policy explicitly allows them. The enforcement date was changed from a previous schedule.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
item.description:
Microsoft describes a malicious extension branded as Claude Code that installs a persistent SSH backdoor, and provides detection and remediation guidance. The post focuses on how the extension behaves and how to identify affected systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Security extension for the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
A new GitHub security extension is available in public preview for the GitHub Copilot app. It lets you review and work through repository code scanning alerts without leaving the app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies
item.description:
Azure Front Door Premium now supports generally available WAF policies at the profile and route level, instead of only at individual domains. This allows broader baseline protection across an entire Front Door profile or selected routes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: .NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates
item.description:
Microsoft released out-of-band .NET security updates in October 2026 to address vulnerabilities in the Brotli decoder and tarball ownership handling. The post is a security notice, not a feature release.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update
item.description:
GitHub’s September 2026 Visual Studio Copilot update adds pull request exploration in chat, support for choosing the AI model your team uses, and package vulnerability fixes surfaced directly from Visual Studio.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Safe Key Rotation
item.description:
Azure Cosmos DB Safe Key Rotation is now generally available. It adds timestamp metadata for when each account key was last used, which helps identify active keys before rotating or retiring credentials.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Updates to GitHub secret scanning
item.description:
GitHub announced updates to secret scanning, including changes to audit log events and bug fixes. The notice specifically mentions a November 12, 2026 change to the business field in affected secret_scanning_alert.* and secret_scanning_push_protection.bypass audit log events.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Service tag match condition for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
item.description:
Service tag match conditions for Azure Front Door Premium WAF custom rules are now generally available. This lets rules match on Azure service tag IP prefix groups.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Keyless TLS on Application Gateway with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
item.description:
Azure Application Gateway now supports keyless TLS termination with certificates stored in Azure Key Vault Managed HSM. During TLS handshakes, signatures are performed inside the HSM and the private key is not exported to the gateway.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub package firewall in public preview
item.description:
GitHub package firewall is now in public preview. It is intended to reduce malware risks during package installation by blocking package-install-time attacks that can steal credentials from CI/CD hosts or developer workstations.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.
item.description:
Microsoft announced new capabilities in Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception aimed at helping organizations contain AI agent risk and continuously adapt protection. The post frames agents as insider-like risks and focuses on security controls that keep pace with their behavior.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: External key management for Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
item.description:
External key management for Azure Key Vault Managed HSM is now generally available in all Azure public regions. It allows organizations with regulatory or sovereignty requirements to keep physical control of key-encryption keys while using Azure services that support this capability.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: AI Scan for pull requests generally available
item.description:
AI Scan for pull requests is now generally available in code scanning. It complements CodeQL by detecting vulnerabilities in pull request changes for languages and frameworks not currently covered by CodeQL.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Cloud HSM hardware audit logging
item.description:
Azure Cloud HSM hardware audit logging is now generally available. It adds hardware-generated audit records for supported HSM management operations to aid security monitoring, compliance, governance, and forensic investigations.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Audit GitHub Code Quality finding dismissals and reopenings
item.description:
GitHub audit logs now include manual dismissals and reopenings of GitHub Code Quality findings at the organization or enterprise level. This lets admins review actions on findings that appear in a repository’s default-branch backlog or other Code Quality views.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
item.description:
Microsoft says organizations should begin testing certificate ecosystems now to prepare for post-quantum authentication. The post highlights Microsoft’s PQC TLS Pilot Program as a way to validate readiness for future post-quantum TLS deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Exceptions in WAF for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door
item.description:
Azure Web Application Firewall exceptions are now generally available for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door. The feature lets customers exclude specific parts of a request from WAF inspection to reduce false positives.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Purpose-built model for leaked secret detection
item.description:
GitHub announced a new purpose-built, context-aware model for leaked secret detection as part of Secret Protection. It is intended to improve secret detection in code workflows, including those that involve AI agents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot now generally available
item.description:
Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot is now generally available. It is supported in GitHub Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: CISO perspectives on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI
item.description:
The post says CISOs should adapt vulnerability management practices for AI-driven environments to reduce cybersecurity risk and improve resilience. It frames the topic as managing vulnerabilities in the age of AI-powered tooling and threats.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Secret scanning adds detectors for Lovable, Supabase, and more
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning added new detectors for secrets from Lovable Labs, Pydantic Services Inc., and Supabase. A new provider also joined the secret scanning partnership program.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire
item.description:
Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing. This reduces the risk of a repository or project name changing after the configuration is created.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rate limits for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
GitHub is adding rate limits for private vulnerability reports to reduce low-quality and automated submissions that can obscure important reports. The change caps how many new reports a single account can submit.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Structured forms for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
Private vulnerability reports now support structured forms to collect the details needed for triage, including a reproducible proof of concept. This replaces reliance on a single free-text field with a more guided intake flow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
item.description:
Microsoft published a brief post pointing readers to highlights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report. The note says the security environment is becoming more interconnected, but provides no detailed findings in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Secure what’s next: Your guide to Microsoft Security at Microsoft Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s Ignite 2026 security post says the company will highlight an AI-first, end-to-end security platform. The platform is described as covering identities, devices, data, applications, clouds, infrastructure, and AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: X25519-only TLS ends for GHE.com on October 7
item.description:
Starting October 7, 2026, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHE.com) will stop accepting TLS connections from clients that support only X25519 for key agreement. Most customers are not expected to be affected.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Require proof of presence for high-impact actions
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports requiring proof of presence before members perform high-impact actions. This adds an interactive re-authentication or MFA challenge on top of the existing sudo-style control.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Microsoft is updating its author-signing certificate starting September 23, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft will update the author-signing certificate used for NuGet packages on September 23, 2026. Users who rely on trusted signer policies or certificate fingerprint verification should add the new certificate before then.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports local sandboxing to limit the impact of unintended commands by restricting access to local files, network resources, and credentials. The feature is configured in the app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
item.description:
Microsoft says EvilTokens emerged as a major phishing-as-a-service platform for device code phishing, using AI-assisted lures, automated infrastructure, and token theft. In collaboration with partners, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted its infrastructure and operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Security improvements for SSH
item.description:
GitHub is updating SSH security by removing several older algorithms, adding a new one, and requiring larger RSA SSH keys. The change tightens supported SSH configurations to improve security.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise adds credential inventory exports
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise now lets enterprise owners export a complete inventory of credentials that can access the enterprise. The export includes SSH keys, classic and fine-grained personal access tokens, OAuth App access tokens, and other credential types.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Network egress controls for hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry public preview now supports network egress controls for hosted agents. Customers can define ordered outbound rules by destination host, including wildcard FQDNs like *.contoso.com, with allow or deny actions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Stage-only npm tokens for safer automation
item.description:
GitHub added a new npm granular access token permission option, Read and write (stage only). It allows automated workflows to stage package versions for review without granting the token full publish access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Payments HSM v2
item.description:
Azure Payments HSM v2 is in public preview. It is a highly available, single-tenant payment HSM service for payment processing, credential issuance, PIN processing, key management, and authentication data protection, with exclusive administrative control retained by the customer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions generally available
item.description:
Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions are now generally available for GitHub Enterprise, organizations, and repositories. The feature lets you define an allowlist to control who can execute workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Hardening Container Storage with Bind Mount Options and EmptyDir Permissions
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 adds alpha support for bind mount options on volume mounts and configurable permission modes for emptyDir volumes. These features let users apply Linux mount flags like noexec, nosuid, and nodev, and set emptyDir modes such as 01777 or 0750 without init-container workarounds.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan no longer requires CodeQL default setup
item.description:
AI Scan for pull requests can now find security vulnerabilities even when CodeQL default setup is not enabled on a repository. Previously, AI Scan for pull requests required CodeQL default setup.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: SHA-1 in HTTPS on GitHub sunset
item.description:
GitHub has completed the scheduled sunset of SHA-1 for HTTPS on github.com and partner services. SHA-1 is now disabled for HTTPS connections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft describes an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonated executives and used fake invoices to target finance teams for ACH payment fraud. The post focuses on the attack pattern and how organizations can protect against it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft Defender is described as detecting and disrupting AI-themed phishing, malware, and multi-stage attacks across the attack chain. The post is a Microsoft Security Blog entry dated 2026-09-10.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: User-bound user delegation SAS for Azure Storage
item.description:
Azure Storage now generally available with user-bound user delegation SAS, combining user delegation SAS flexibility with Entra ID user-bound access for stronger authentication. The update adds enhanced secure authentication for Azure Storage.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: npm extends recovery-code security holds to all accounts
item.description:
npm now applies a 72-hour security hold to any account after a successful recovery-code sign-in. The hold was previously limited to high-impact accounts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.0 adds support for Linux ARM64
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.0 is available on Linux ARM64. The release also adds a new Rust security query, expands framework coverage for Java/Kotlin and C#, and includes analysis accuracy improvements across multiple languages.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Threat matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Cloud Web Applications Threat Matrix, a MITRE ATT&CK-aligned framework for understanding and prioritizing threats against cloud-hosted web applications and serverless platforms. It is intended to help defenders map attacks and identify mitigations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Block pull requests with exposed secrets from merging
item.description:
GitHub added a repository ruleset capability to prevent pull requests from merging when they introduce exposed secrets. This extends rulesets as a repository-wide protection mechanism.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
item.description:
Microsoft says edge AI deployments in customer-owned environments require stronger verification of systems, software, and AI assets before sharing sensitive data, credentials, or models. The post frames secure edge AI as a trust and validation problem for third-party environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: KubeletInUserNamespace (aka Rootless mode) Graduates to Beta
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 moves KubeletInUserNamespace to beta and enables the feature gate by default. It allows node components to run as a non-root user in a Linux user namespace, reducing host impact from node-component exploits, while leaving existing rootful clusters unchanged unless explicitly configured.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: security: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion
item.description:
Microsoft reports that invisible Unicode characters, previously used in AI prompt injection, are now being used to hide words from email filters as part of phishing evasion. The technique relies on obfuscating text before parsers process it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies
item.description:
Azure Front Door Web Application Firewall (WAF) now supports associating WAF policies at the profile and route levels in public preview. This lets you apply baseline protection across a profile and more targeted policies on specific routes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Counterfeit installers to system compromise: Tracking a deceptive software download campaign
item.description:
Microsoft describes an active malware campaign that uses fake software download pages and repackaged installer archives to impersonate legitimate vendors. The post includes observed tactics, Defender XDR detections, indicators of compromise, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Confidential VMs for Azure Linux
item.description:
Confidential Virtual Machines for Azure Linux in AKS are now generally available. This adds CVM node pool support for migrating highly sensitive container workloads to AKS.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Your agent’s guardrails have a bypass
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Agent Hooks, an open, framework-neutral governance contract for agent systems. It includes conformance testing and is intended to make enforcement fail closed instead of failing open when controls crash.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: ​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: August 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s August 2026 security update highlights new capabilities for monitoring agent activity, broader security coverage across supported environments, and improved security management across environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Bastion shareable link expiration
item.description:
Azure Bastion shareable links now support an administrator-defined expiration date and time. After expiration, the link can no longer be used to connect.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Connect to AKS clusters using Azure Bastion
item.description:
Azure Bastion integration with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is now generally available. It lets customers create a secure tunnel from a local machine through Azure Bastion to an AKS cluster API server.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Custom block response code and body for Application Gateway WAF
item.description:
Azure WAF on Application Gateway is now generally available with support for custom block response status codes and response bodies for blocked requests. This lets you define the HTTP response returned when WAF blocks a request.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code scanning adds a mitigated alert dismissal reason
item.description:
Code scanning now supports dismissing alerts with the reason “Mitigated” when the vulnerability still exists in code but is offset by external controls, such as a web application firewall or network protections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the Frost Radar™: Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a visionary leader in Frost & Sullivan’s 2026 Frost Radar for Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, citing Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s unified runtime security. The post is a brief recognition announcement with no product changes described.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Credential revocation and deauthorization by token type
item.description:
GitHub added self-service incident response actions to deauthorize and revoke user credentials by token type and by specific user. The update extends existing credential revocation workflows for security incidents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple redirect URIs and token refresh for OAuth apps
item.description:
GitHub updated OAuth app and GitHub App platform support to improve app security. The changes include optional expiring access tokens with refresh tokens for OAuth apps, and support for multiple redirect URIs.

  • Source: GitHub
